correctness.rationale: The signed descent at index zero is included. An independent coefficientwise proof follows by comparing the power-series Worpitzky expansion with (1+t)^n=((1-t)+2t)^n. The j=0 and j=1 terms agree exactly. At j=2, the difference is 2n(n-1)t(1-t)^(n-2), since the ordinary Eulerian polynomial at j=2 is 1+t. For j>=3, both expansions have terms divisible by 2^(2+v2(n(n-1))): write binom(n,j)=n(n-1)binom(n-2,j-2)/(j(j-1)) and use v2(j(j-1))<=j-2. This applies even at n=2 when there is no tail. It proves the modulus and proves exactness at coefficient t; the signed Worpitzky formula separately gives B(n,1)=3^n-n-1. For n=2^r the error vanishes modulo 2^(r+1) while every interior Pascal valuation is r-v2(k), by oddness of binom(2^r-1,k-1). Counting indices of each valuation gives 2^(j-1) and the endpoints are 1. Independently ran python3 /workspace/review_evidence/recompute_arithmetic.py: direct Worpitzky coefficient comparison through n=64, signed-word enumeration through n=6, and full interior valuation/multiplicity checks in powers of two through 64. The frozen n<=512 diagnostic is recorded evidence, not a replay or the proof.
